hero.caption: Ruins of the Paikuli tower. This is the western wall; the middle Persian version of the inscriptions was used here. The stone blocks which were used to build the tower are scattered all around the monument; these stone blocks bear no inscriptions. Nikon D610 with an AF DX Fisheye-Nikkor 10.5mm f/2.8G ED lens. March 2015.

images.filename: Recently discovered f1 Parthian script, inscribed rounded stone block from the Paikuli Tower of Narseh, Sulaymaniyah Museum.jpg
images.caption: Recently discovered (by an Italian archaeological team from the Sapienza University of Rome) f1, Parthian inscription, stone from the Paikuli Tower of the Sassanian king Narseh. It is flanked by 2 other inscribed stone blocks. Note the holes on the surfaces; these were for joining the stones. C. 293 CE. From the Paikuli Tower of Narseh, near Barkal Village, Sulaymaniyah Governorate, Iraq. Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq. This image was taken in 2015 while the stones were in storage; they have been on display within the Paikuli Gallery since June 2019.
